notes: Lock chances are percent per doorway SEGMENT (the shared edge between two cells),
keyed by rank and orientation. Values over 100 mean guaranteed-locked at bias 1.
The sim rolls a segment when the first door on it is placed (the real game rolls
lazily on first click); see README 'Known simplifications'.
Named gap: the Silver Key used on a Secret Passage doorway is consumed and its
cross/t-layout bias (state.special.silver_key_draft) is set, but Game.open_door
resolves the Secret Passage's own colour pick (Phase.COLOUR_PENDING) before any
deal happens, and draft.py's colour-selective draw does not consult the bias flag
-- so the bias is silently discarded on that one doorway type. The wiki settles
only the Prism Key's Secret-Passage interaction ('the Prism Key takes priority and
the Secret Passage's chosen color is ignored'), not the Silver Key's; not fixed here.
Named gap: special key 'warping' (e.g. a Great Hall side door that unlocks with no
following draft, sending the player straight to a different room) is unmodellable
as this engine is structured -- Game.open_door always deals a hand once a locked
segment resolves open, with no code path that skips straight to placement. Not built.

lock_chance.comment: ew_by_rank: E-W doors within a rank. ns_boundary: N-S doors, keyed by the LOWER rank of the boundary; 'edge' = cols 0/4, 'center' = cols 1-3. Ranks 1-3 are never locked by chance.

bias.comment: Daily lock-bias multiplier: effective chance = base * bias, bias starts at 1. Locked door: bias = min(bias + locked_delta, 1) unless chance was over high_second_roll_above and a second base-chance roll passes. Unlocked door: bias = max(bias + unlocked_delta, 1) unless chance was under low_second_roll_below and a second base-chance roll fails.

always_unlocked_rooms.comment: Doors of these rooms are guaranteed unlocked and bypass the bias system (Corridor; Corriyard, the Courtyard upgrade whose doors are always unlocked and never security).

always_locked_rooms.comment: Doors of these rooms are guaranteed locked and bypass the bias system, mirroring always_unlocked_rooms (Great Hall: 'all seven of these doors are guaranteed to be locked'). The room's own entry doorway is never touched -- roll_segment only ever sees fresh, non-entry segments. side_search_cost prices the two side doorways: each hides its actual passage behind 3 inner doors (the far doorway has no such search). The wiki's theoretical per-door-type table (Doorway column, each half of the room): center 50%, each of 2 edges 25%. Opening doors in the optimal order (center first, an edge second, the last forced) costs 1 key on a correct first try (p=0.50), 2 on a correct second try (p=0.25), 3 when forced to the third (p=0.25) -- expectation 1.75 keys. side_search_cost stores that distribution as EXTRA keys beyond the base 1 already charged for opening a locked segment: 0 extra (found it first, p=0.50), 1 extra (found it second, p=0.25), 2 extra (forced third, p=0.25); 1*0.50 + 2*0.25 + 3*0.25 reproduces the 1.75 total. Rolled once per side doorway segment, like every other lock roll.

side_search_cost.comment: Parallel arrays: extra_keys[i] is charged with probability weights[i] (weights need not sum to 100, but do here).

security.comment: A freshly placed whitelisted room's doors may spawn as security doors: requires spawned-today < spawn_limit[level], door distance to the Antechamber center <= distance_cutoff (cell centers 10 units apart), a uniform(0, distance_roll_max) roll strictly above that distance, then the per-room chance (forced to 100 on high security). room_door_chance collapses the datamined per-door Left/Forward/Right table to each room's strongest door (confidence: datamined, simplified).

keycard.comment: Chance (percent) of finding the Keycard on first entry to a source room; the card is permanent for the day and never consumed. Source list from the wiki's spawn locations restricted to rooms modeled in the sim; the per-room chance is not datamined (confidence: inferred).

special_key_menu.comment: The published fixed row order of the locked-door special-keys menu (Special_keys/Menu_keys template, 'the special keys menu always lists keys in a fixed order'), regardless of pickup order or which are held -- a data table, not a Python constant. env/actions.py's LOCK_SPECIAL_KEY_BASE range indexes this array 1:1. secret_garden_key and key_8 are modelled in this sim as draft_conditions tags rather than door keys (see their effects/items modules) -- both are reserved slots, permanently masked off in the action mask rather than removed, so their ids never shift if a later PR wires them up. basement_key's own fits() is also always False here: this sim models the Basement purely as an off-grid area-graph destination (docs/areas.md's basement_key_foundation/basement_key_well gates), so no on-grid DOOR_LOCKED segment is ever a basement door (Doors wiki page: 'any normal or special key other than a Basement Key does not fit' a basement door, and the converse also holds -- a Basement Key does not fit an ordinary locked door). prism_key fits a held-and-colour-fitting room (Bedroom/Hallway/Green Room/Shop/Red Room) and colour-restricts the resulting draft on use (special_items.json's implemented:true, effects/items/prism_key.py).
